subject: Autoscale burst governor pricing proposal and contract path
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@cloudata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Autoscale burst governor pricing proposal and contract path

Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our call, I’m putting a concise proposal for Dedicated capacity + the autoscale/burst add-on behavior that CloudData asked about so you have something to take to your procurement team. High-level: you’d reserve a 40-GPU pool (A100-equivalent) for predictable throughput and attach an autoscale "governor" that allows short-lived spikes up to 65 GPUs with a cooldown policy to prevent sustained overuse.

Proposal (starter):
- Reserved commit: 40 GPUs (A100-eq) — $48,000 / month (12-month term) — 15% volume discount applied.
- Burst governor: allow bursts +25 GPUs (to 65 total) with a per-GPU-hour surge rate of $3.75 for each GPU-hour beyond the reserved pool.
- Burst limits: max continuous burst window = 3 hours; soft daily cap = 8 GPU-hours beyond commit.
- Cooldown: after any burst > 60 minutes, governor enforces a minimum cooldown of 45 minutes before another burst.
- Throughput guarantee: 40 GPUs reserved = baseline sustained throughput of ~320K tokens/min with p99 latency target < 150ms on short prompt workloads; fallback routing to smaller quantized variants if unmet.

Attached is a worksheet (rdw-dedicated-burst-worksheet-v2.xlsx) with modeling for your peak pattern that we discussed. Next steps: if this looks close, Marissa will approve a commercial exception for the discount and we’ll send a short addendum for signature. If procurement wants a capped monthly spend rather than per-hour surge, we can propose a burst credit slab instead — modeled on sheet tab B.

Thanks — I’ll hold next Tue/Thu for a quick sync.

—
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0191

Redwood Inference — Serving runtime for production LLMs

Subject: Re: Autoscale burst governor pricing proposal and contract path

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful and close to what we expected. A few clarifying Qs from procurement and engineering:

1) How deterministic is the p99 latency guarantee across multi-tenant hosted nodes vs dedicated? We need to ensure production job queues (ETL + user-facing completions) don't compete unpredictably.
2) Can the burst governor be configured by route (so only model A gets bursts but our embedding pipeline stays on reserved capacity)?
3) We prefer a monthly capped exposure rather than pure per-GPU-hour billing. Can you show an equivalent burst-credit slab (e.g., 200 GPU-hours/month at a blended rate) we can commit to?
4) If we exceed soft daily cap repeatedly, what's the escalation path? Are there auto-throttle options vs hard-deny?

Procurement note: 12-month term OK but we’ll ask for an early-exit clause tied to gross-usage thresholds for the first 90 days. I’m looping them in on the cc to start the formal review.

Appreciate the quick modeling — can you get Monica on a call to confirm the enforcement mechanics?

—
Alicia Ramos
Director, ML Platform, CloudData Inc.
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@cloudata.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, CloudData Procurement <procurement@cloudata.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Autoscale burst governor pricing proposal and contract path

Hi Alicia —

Thanks — answered inline and attached a quick alternative slab model in the worksheet (tab C):

1) Determinism: Dedicated pools are single-tenant for the reserved commit; the burst governor uses your same dedicated pool and spins up additional dedicated nodes drawn from a shared burst capacity pool that we can reserve for you as part of the add-on (optional). If you keep burst capacity as shared multiservice, p99 can vary up to ~30–40ms in our internal tests for very bursty tail workloads; reserving a burst buffer reduces that delta to <10ms. We can include a clause to guarantee p99 within +/- 25ms of baseline when burst buffer is reserved.

2) Route-level controls: yes — the governor supports policy per route/model. We can pin embedding pipelines to the reserved pool and only allow inference routes (completion) to consume bursts.

3) Monthly capped exposure: see tab C — example slab: 200 burst GPU-hours / month at a blended $2.95/GPU-hour = $590/month in excess credit with overage at $4.50/GPU-hour. This gives procurement a predictable cap while allowing headroom.

4) Exceeding soft caps: governor supports graded responses — first, soft throttling (queueing with delayed tokens), then a configurable hard cap if you elect to deny. For escalations we propose automated alerts + a human-runback policy: after 3 soft-cap exceedances in 30 days, an account review triggers and Marissa will assess commercial remediation (credits or increased commit).

I’ve attached rdw-dedicated-burst-worksheet-v2.xlsx with the slab numbers and a suggested addendum language for the p99 guardrail. Monica — any technical notes you want me to fold into the addendum?

—
Karthik

Subject: Re: Autoscale burst governor pricing proposal and contract path

Hi Alicia —

Quick technical confirmation from the infra side:
- Burst enforcement: the governor tracks per-route KV cache and request tokens; when a burst is triggered we first attempt to allocate pre-warmed nodes with matching quantization profile. If pre-warmed nodes are unavailable we fallback to a compatible quantized variant which may increase per-token latency by ~10–20% (we call this "compatible fallback").
- Cooldown enforcement: implemented as a sliding-window counter with a configurable cooldown timer. For your proposal (45-minute cooldown) this is enforced at the allocation layer; it does not drop your in-flight requests but will refuse further allocations until cooldown completes.
- Observability: we emit burst metrics (GPU-hours consumed, burst_count, cooldown_active boolean) to the Console and can push a daily webhook to your internal PagerDuty/Slack channel.

Operational recommendation: if you have two distinct workloads (interactive completions + heavy nightly ETL), pin the ETL to a separate reserved pool and only permit interactive routes to burst. That avoids noisy neighbor effects and keeps the p99 tail tight.

If procurement wants contract language, Karthik/Marissa can share the addendum; from an SRE POV I’d sign off on the 3-hour continuous burst and 45-minute cooldown.

—
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Karthik / Monica / Marissa —

Thanks for the detail and for adding the slab alternative. Procurement is comfortable with the 12-month term if we can:
- Move to the 200 GPU-hour month slab at $2.95/GPU-hour with $4.50 overage.
- Add the p99 guardrail language for reserved burst buffer (<=25ms delta) when a reserved burst buffer is paid for.
- Include a 90-day early-exit conditional if monthly aggregate consumption stays >35% below the committed baseline for 60 consecutive days.

We’ll attach a PO if you can send an addendum and a short SOW describing the burst governor behavior (the one-pager is fine). Also please include the worksheet and the redline-friendly PDF so procurement can route.

If you can circulate the two documents today we’ll queue signature next week.
